evidence.sourceExcerpt: CRAN: Package fedmatch fedmatch: Fast, Flexible, and User-Friendly Record Linkage Methods Provides a flexible set of tools for matching two un-linked data sets. 'fedmatch' allows for three ways to match data: exact matches, fuzzy matches, and multi-variable matches. It also allows an easy combination of these three matches via the tier matching function. For the full license information see the Copernicus Regulation . Publications, models and data products that make use of these datasets must include proper acknowledgement, including citing datasets and the journal article as in the following citation. Citation Jean-Francois Pekel, Andrew Cottam, Noel Gorelick, Alan S. Belward, High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes. Nature 540, 418-422 (2016). (doi:10.1038/nature20584) If you are using the data as a layer in a published map, please include the following attribution text: 'Source: EC JRC/Google' Data Users Guide For a description of all of the datasets and details on how to use the data please see the Data Users Guide . Data Update Notes (1984–2024) We have updated the Global Surface Water Explorer dataset to include recent years. Please note the following key details regarding this new release: Collection 2 Transition: To extend our previous dataset (which ended in 2021), we transitioned to Landsat Collection 2. Collection 2 improves the absolute geolocation accuracy of the Landsat archive relative to Collection 1, principally through re-baselining the ground control library to the Sentinel-2 Global Reference Image. Combining scenes from the two collections therefore introduces a residual co-registration offset between them. The magnitude of this offset is spatially variable, reflecting the regionally uneven improvement of the ground control: it is typically sub-pixel but can reach or exceed one 30 m pixel in certain WRS-2 path/rows, while remaining negligible where the Collection 1 control was already accurate (Crawford et al., 2023) . A complete backprocessing to ensure full consistency of the archive is planned. Layer Coverage & Merging: Long-term summary products—such as Occurrence, Recurrence, and Transitions—synthesize the entire time series from 1984 to 2024. However, the Seasonality, Monthly History, and Yearly History assets only cover the 2022–2024 period. To get the complete historical timeline for these specific assets, you will need to merge them with our previous historical assets (e.g., Version 1.4). Seasonality Improvements: We have entirely recomputed the Seasonality layers from 2016 to 2021 (still based on Landsat Collection 1) to correct a known issue that occasionally overestimated seasonal surface water. Meanwhile, the 2022–2024 Seasonality layers have been computed using the updated Landsat Collection 2. YearlyHistory Updates: changes in the 2016-2021 Seasonality assets are now reflected into the YearlyHistory_2016_2021. Occurrence Improvements: In versions 1.2 to 1.4, the years added after the original release (v1.0) were not processed in a way fully consistent with the original Occurrence calculation, which introduced errors. To restore consistency with the original dataset, the added years have been reprocessed against the v1.0 baseline. The corrected Occurrence layer is provided in GSW v1.5, computed on Landsat Collection 1 from 1984 to 2021 and on Collection 2 thereafter. Monthly Recurrence: An issue has been identified in the Monthly Recurrence in v1.4 (2021) and v1.5 (2024) layer, which can lower the long-term monthly values where observations are sparse. The correction has not yet been carried out and is foreseen. Delivery Mechanisms All of the datasets that comprise the Global Surface Water 1984-2021 and the recent 2022-2024 are being made freely available using the following delivery mechanisms: Global Surface Water Explorer, Data Download, Google Earth Engine and Web Map Services.
